summary: The top of the content area — the page's name, what it is for, and the rule under both.

figma.note: Not drawn in Figma yet. Built in code from the App shell Rules (40000390:30181), which place the page title and page actions in the page header inside the content area. The App shell page's own 'Page heading' is a text node standing in for this component.

measurementsFrom: docs/foundations/typography.md (heading/xl is the page-title step) and the App shell Rules

pairs.dont: Give every panel on the page its own PageHeader.
pairs.do: One PageHeader at the top; sections below are headings, not page headers.
pairs.why: The component renders the page's h1, and a page has one. A second one tells a screen reader the page started again, and visually it sets two things at 30px competing to be the name of the screen. Section titles are heading/lg on an h2.

pairs.dont: Put the page title in the 48 top bar next to the breadcrumb.
pairs.do: Leave the bar to the sidebar toggle and the breadcrumb, and name the page here.
pairs.why: The bar is the same 48 on every screen in the product. Everything added to it competes with the breadcrumb, which is the one thing that says where you are — and the title repeats what the last breadcrumb item already said.

pairs.dont: Write "This page shows information about your notification settings."
pairs.do: Say what is in scope and what changing it does — or leave the description out.
pairs.why: A description that restates the title costs a line and a reading pause and returns nothing. The ones worth having answer a question the title raises: what does this cover, when does it take effect, who does it reach.

pairs.dont: Let the description run the width of a fluid dashboard.
pairs.do: Nothing — it caps itself at the reading width, 768.
pairs.why: A fluid page hands the column 2256 at a 2560 monitor. A line of prose that long is hard to track back to its start, which is why width="reading" exists for forms; the cap is on the description so a dashboard does not have to choose between a wide grid and a readable sentence.

pairs.dont: Keep the rule when a full-bleed table or a single card starts 24 below it.
pairs.do: divider={false} where the next thing already has a top edge.
pairs.why: Two horizontal lines 24 apart with nothing between them read as a mistake rather than as structure. The rule is there to separate the page's name from the page; when the page starts with its own border, that separation is already drawn.

a11y: The title is the page's <h1>, and the only one. Section titles below are <h2> at heading/lg.

PageHeader renders a <header>, but it sits inside AppShellContent's <main>, where <header> is a generic element rather than a second banner. The banner is AppShellHeader. Put PageHeader outside the content area and you get two banners.
The rule is a border on the header, not an <hr>, so nothing is announced for a line that carries no meaning of its own.
